chapters.title: Identity Provider Authentication with OpenID Connect

blocks.text: Omnisient supports authentication through your organization's Identity Provider (IdP). This means your team can securely access Omnisient using their existing company credentials.

By integrating with your Identity Provider via OpenID Connect (OIDC), Omnisient allows your organization to centrally manage authentication. This keeps access control, password policies, and user revocations within your own security environment.

This approach provides a consistent and secure login experience for users, simplifies access management for administrators, and ensures that authentication always follows your organization's internal security policies.
Key terminology

rows: The process of confirming that a user is who they say they are. For example, entering a username and password or using multi-factor authentication (MFA).
MFA adds an extra layer of security to the login process by requiring users to provide two or more forms of verification before they can sign in.

Once a user is authenticated, authorization determines what they're allowed to do. In Omnisient's case, authentication is handled by your Identity Provider, while authorization (what a user can access inside Omnisient) is managed through Omnisient roles and permissions.

A feature that allows users to access multiple applications using one set of login credentials. With SSO, your team can sign in once to their Identity Provider and automatically gain access to Omnisient and other connected systems without needing to log in separately each time.

The service that handles authentication for your organization. It verifies user credentials and sends confirmation back to Omnisient. Examples: Microsoft Azure Entra, Okta, Google Workspace, Ping Identity.
A secure standard that lets applications (like Omnisient) use an external identity system to verify who a user is. It builds on top of OAuth 2.0, adding an identity layer for authentication.
Small bits of secure data sent between systems to prove your identity.

blocks.text: What is an Identity Provider (IdP)?

Your Identity Provider (IdP) is the system that manages all your organization's users and logins. When configured as an authentication method, your IdP is responsible for telling Omnisient that this person is who they say they are.
Using an IdP means you stay in control by adding or removing users in one place, and it then automatically applies to Omnisient too.
Common examples of IdPs are Microsoft Entra, Okta, Google Workspace and Ping Identity.
What is OpenID Connect (OIDC)?
OpenID Connect (OIDC) is an authentication layer built on top of the OAuth 2.0 security standard.
It allows users to sign in to Omnisient using their existing company credentials instead of a separate Omnisient password.
This approach makes authentication:

items: More secure, because passwords and policies are managed centrally by your organization.
Simpler for users, since there's no need to remember multiple passwords.
More compliant, as your organization can enforce its own MFA and access rules.

blocks.text: How OIDC works in Omnisient
Here's a quick look at what happens during sign-in:

items: The user opens the Omnisient login page.
Omnisient detects their organization and redirects them to the configured IdP.
The IdP authenticates the user.
The IdP sends a secure token back to Omnisient.
Omnisient validates the token and logs the user in.

blocks.text: Note: The user must already exist in Omnisient but Omnisient won't handle the password. Authentication happens entirely through the IdP.
Configuring OIDC to authenticate with your IdP
To connect your organization's IdP with Omnisient using OIDC, we'll need a few key details from your IdP setup.
Who can provide this information?
The information below is typically provided by someone who manages your organization's identity or security systems such as:

items: Your IT Administrator,
A Security or Compliance Manager, or
Anyone responsible for your organization's SSO or Identity Provider configuration.

blocks.text: If you're unsure who this is, reach out to your internal IT or Security team and they'll be able to retrieve these details from your IdP.
Information required from your IdP
Here's what we'll need to set up OpenID Connect for your organization.

rows: The unique URL that identifies your IdP.
Used to verify the authenticity of tokens sent by your IdP.
A standard OIDC endpoint (usually ending in /.well-known/openid-configuration) that provides metadata about your IdP.
Allows Omnisient to automatically discover your IdP's configuration details and endpoints.
A unique identifier for Omnisient within your IdP.
Generated when you register Omnisient as a new application in your IdP.
Tells the IdP which app is requesting authentication.
A secure key created in your IdP to authenticate Omnisient's requests.
Created alongside the Client ID during app registration.
Ensures communication between Omnisient and your IdP is secure and trusted.
Defines the information Omnisient can request from your IdP (commonly openid email profile).
Allows Omnisient to receive the user's verified identity details.

blocks.text: Best practices for managing your IdP
Keep access management centralized

items: Manage access only through your IdP. All user access, whether adding, removing, or suspending users, should happen in your organization's IdP. This keeps control centralized and ensures any changes automatically apply to Omnisient.
Don't manually share login credentials or create shared Omnisient accounts. Each user should have their own identity managed through the IdP.

blocks.text: Use guest or external user management for partners

items: If you need to grant access to external collaborators or contractors, add them as guests in your IdP.
This keeps all access requests, MFA policies, and audit trails under your organization's security policies.
You can revoke their access easily and immediately when their work ends.
Most IdPs (like Entra and Okta) support secure guest user functionality that works seamlessly with OIDC.

blocks.text: Using OpenID Connect with your organization's Identity Provider allows you to manage authentication to Omnisient through your own secure systems. This setup ensures that:

items: Access is controlled and monitored by your organization.
Authentication follows your internal password and MFA policies.
User access can be granted or revoked centrally through your IdP.

Our team will guide you through the required details and help ensure everything is configured securely and correctly.

blocks.text: Organization security settings

The Organization Security Settings page gives organizations control over who can sign in to Omnisient and how, in line with their own security standards. Organization owners can view and configure authentication through either an external Identity Provider (IdP) or local authentication managed within Omnisient.
1. Identity Provider authentication
Your organization can choose to use an Identity Provider (IdP) such as Microsoft Entra, Okta, or Google Workspace to handle user authentication into Omnisient.
When Identity Provider authentication is enabled:

items: Users are redirected to your organization's IdP login page instead of entering a password directly into Omnisient.
Authentication is handled by your IdP following your organization's password policies, MFA, and access controls.
Access can be granted or revoked directly from your IdP, keeping security management centralized.

blocks.text: Once configured, users within your organization will log in using their existing company credentials, ensuring a consistent and secure login experience.
1.1 OpenID Connect (OIDC)

Omnisient currently supports connecting to your Identity Provider (IdP) using OpenID Connect (OIDC): a secure, industry-standard method for enabling authentication through your organization's chosen IdP.
When configured, OIDC allows Omnisient to rely on your organization's IdP to verify users' identities and grant access securely.

Note: OpenID Connect (OIDC) requires configuration. Your organization's IT or security administrator will need to provide specific details from your Identity Provider to enable this connection. For detailed guidance on what's needed and how to set it up, see the chapter Identity Provider Authentication with OpenID Connect.
2. Locally managed authentication
Omnisient also supports locally managed authentication, allowing users to sign in directly using:

items: Their Omnisient username and password, or
An existing Microsoft account

blocks.text: This method is ideal for organizations that don't yet have a centralized Identity Provider or prefer to manage user access directly within Omnisient.
Note: Microsoft account login is a convenience feature for individual users and is not the same as connecting Omnisient to a Microsoft Entra Identity Provider.
User settings: Profile
The Profile section allows you to manage your individual user information. Here you can view or update your personal details:

items: First Name and Last Name: Editable fields you can update at any time.
Mobile Number: Optional, but editable for your convenience.
Default Company: If you're assigned to more than one company, you'll see a dropdown to select your default. This option is hidden for single-company users.
Email Address: This field is always read-only for all users. However, if you wish to edit this aspect of your organization, please contact Support for assistance.

blocks.text: User security settings
This section allows you to update your password. You'll be asked to provide:

items: Your current password
A new password that meets the password policy set out below
Confirm the new password

blocks.text: Changing your password regularly makes your account safer.
Session timeout

The platform is designed to log users out after 15 minutes of inactivity. Inactivity means no mouse or keyboard input, so a browser tab left open on its own will time out. The 15 minute limit is fixed and cannot be changed per organization.

Signing out ends the session on the server rather than only in the browser. Duplicate sessions are blocked: if you try to sign in while a session is already active, you will get an error and will not be able to enter the platform on the duplicate.
Pages excluded from the timeout
On the pages below, the session stays active even when the user isn't clicking or typing. This lets long-running work finish without being interrupted:

items: SQLPad
Jupyter notebooks
Project pages (any page inside a project)
Admin reports
Project report viewer

blocks.text: Password policy
A password must be a minimum of 12 characters and include at least one lower case character, one upper case character, one digit, and one special character.
To enable 2FA, your company must contact Omnisient to request activation on your account. This guide outlines the steps involved in setting up 2FA after it's enabled by Omnisient Support.
Requesting 2FA activation

To activate 2FA, an authorized representative from your company should reach out to your Omnisient Account Manager or send a request to support@omnisient.com. Once activated, 2FA setup will be accessible from your account's security settings.
Prerequisites

items: A smartphone with an authenticator app installed, such as Microsoft Authenticator.
Access to your Omnisient account login credentials.

blocks.text: Step-by-step instructions
1. Log into your Omnisient account

items: Visit app.omnisient.com and log in using your username and password.

blocks.text: 2. Scan the QR code

items: Open your authenticator app.
Scan the QR code displayed on the Omnisient platform.

blocks.text: 3. Enter the 6-digit code

items: After scanning, your authenticator app will generate a 6-digit code.
Enter this code on Omnisient to complete the 2FA setup.

blocks.text: Important tips

items: Device Management: If you switch devices, you may need to disable and re-enable 2FA with your new device promptly.

blocks.text: Troubleshooting

items: Incorrect Code Error: Ensure your device's time settings are accurate, as authenticator apps rely on synchronized time.
Lost Access to Authenticator App: Use a backup code or contact Omnisient Support for assistance.

blocks.text: Admins manage who has access to the Omnisient platform. From here you can invite new users, edit their details and permissions, and deactivate users who no longer need access.

Client Admins are responsible for managing User and Admin user access to match their organization's requirements. Users can be added or removed at the Admin's discretion or as access needs change, and Omnisient provides the functionality for Admins to do this.
Permissions: Only users with Admin permissions can access Users.
Where to find Users
In the Omnisient platform, go to Admin > Users. The Users page lists all the users in your company.
Adding a user to the Omnisient platform

items: Go to Admin > Users.
Click + Add User.
Fill in their details.
Click Add User.

blocks.text: The new user receives a welcome email with:

items: A link to set a secure password
A link to download and install Desktop Connect
Their login email and instructions for logging in to the platform and Desktop Connect
A link to the Help Center for further guidance

blocks.text: Editing a user

items: Go to Admin > Users.
Open the actions menu next to the user and select Edit.
Update their details.

blocks.text: Deactivating a user

items: Go to Admin > Users.
Open the actions menu next to the user and select Deactivate.
Confirm in the dialog that appears.

blocks.text: Deactivation can't be undone, so if you're deactivating your own account as an Admin, make sure another Admin is available first. Doing so immediately removes your access to the platform and Desktop Connect.
Editing a user's permissions

items: Go to Admin > Users.
Open the actions menu next to the user and select Edit Permissions.
Select / deselect relevant permissions.

blocks.text: As different companies may have varying roles and responsibilities, users with Admin privileges can configure permissions according to their specific requirements. Admin users can modify the profiles of user-type users, restricting their access to only the functions that are relevant to their responsibilities.

By granting different levels of access and allowing Admin users to customize permissions, the Omnisient platform ensures that each user has tailored access to the necessary features and functionalities based on their role within the company.

blocks.text: Admin

The Activity Log is an audit trail of account activity across the Omnisient platform, recording what happened, who did it, and when. Admins can see user actions and permission changes directly, without needing to ask Omnisient.
Permissions: Only users with Admin permissions can access the Activity Log.
Where to find Activity Log
In the Omnisient platform, go to Admin > Activity Log.
How Activity Log works
Every entry in the Activity Log includes four fields:

rows: The specific detail of that action
The email address of the user who performed it

blocks.text: Actions

rows: Narrow the log to the last 1, 2, or 3 months.
Export to CSV. The export includes all four fields (Action, Activity, User, Date) for the selected date range.

blocks.text: Auditing platform users

Access reviews are your organization's responsibility. Omnisient does not perform them on your behalf. An audit of the users on the platform can be carried out at any time by your own Admins, using the Admin > Users section together with the Admin > Activity Log. The platform imposes no fixed schedule, so the timing and frequency of reviews is for your organization to set.

Admin > Users shows the current state: who has access today and the permissions each person holds. Admin > Activity Log shows the history: what changed, who changed it, and when. Together, they let an Admin confirm that the right people have access and trace how that access came about.
